record.title: JustMem reports adaptive long-term memory access with higher benchmark accuracy and lower model-token use
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces JustMem, a long-term conversational-memory system that adapts retrieval breadth and source-reading fidelity to each query. In author-run tests using GPT-4.1-mini across LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, it reports the best mean accuracy among the compared memory systems while using fewer generative-model tokens. Results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The authors published the JustMem preprint on arXiv on 2026-09-17.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, the authors report that JustMem had the highest mean accuracy and retrieval recall among the compared memory systems, with 79.61% accuracy on LoCoMo and 83.40% on LongMemEval-S.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Against LightMem, the strongest comparison by mean accuracy on LoCoMo, the authors report 50.7% lower memory-construction tokens and 67.2% lower query-time tokens on LoCoMo, and 64.9% and 55.7% reductions respectively on LongMemEval-S.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the 401-question cognitive split of LoCoMo-Plus, the authors report 62.59% accuracy for JustMem versus 31.67% for MemOS, the strongest baseline in that comparison.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper states that evaluation is limited to established long-term conversational memory benchmarks and a specific memory/retrieval configuration; its efficiency analysis primarily counts generative-model tokens and omits other system-level computation.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the benchmark results or reported token costs was identified.
No public implementation was located during this review, preventing direct inspection of retrieval, source-recovery and planner behavior.
The principal efficiency comparison reports generative tokens but not total system-level compute, latency, energy or dollar cost.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains generalize, query-adaptive evidence retrieval could improve multi-session conversational memory and reduce model-token use. Score 4 reflects a meaningful memory-design result while the evidence remains limited to author-run benchmarks and reported token accounting.
limitations: All quantitative results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
The main comparisons use selected long-term conversational-memory benchmarks and a specific configuration; generality to other memory tasks and model stacks is unknown.
On LoCoMo, the reported paired comparison against LightMem is not statistically significant (p=0.532).
Token accounting excludes embeddings, reranking and other system-level computation, so lower generative-token use does not establish lower total latency, energy or cost.
The authors identify privacy, retention, access-control and sensitive-information leakage risks from stored memories and provenance-based source recovery.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces JustMem, a long-term conversational-memory system that adapts retrieval breadth and source-reading fidelity to each query. In author-run tests using GPT-4.1-mini across LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, it reports the best mean accuracy among the compared memory systems while using fewer generative-model tokens. Results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

technical.claimed_result: Using GPT-4.1-mini for memory construction, planning, answering and LLM judging, the authors report 79.61% mean accuracy on LoCoMo and 83.40% on LongMemEval-S, with the highest compared-system mean accuracy and retrieval recall on both. They report lower generative-token budgets than comparison memory systems, and 62.59% accuracy on the LoCoMo-Plus cognitive split.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports generative-model token counts for construction and online inference; embedding, reranking, offline evaluation and other system-level compute are excluded from its principal efficiency accounting.
technical.demonstrated_result: A public preprint describes the system, benchmark protocol and reported tables. No independent execution or reproduction of its results was performed.
technical.mechanism: JustMem stores compact atomic memories with provenance links, predicts query evidence demands, then chooses local Lookup, broader Compose retrieval, or provenance-based Replay of source conversations. Compose broadens the candidate search while keeping the compact evidence budget fixed; Replay recovers full source context only for fidelity-sensitive queries.
technical.novelty: The paper's proposed distinction between discovery breadth and reading fidelity is its own framing; priority relative to all recent memory systems was not independently established.
technical.regime: Author-reported experiments on LoCoMo (1,540 questions), LongMemEval-S (500 questions), and the 401-question cognitive split of LoCoMo-Plus. Primary benchmark comparisons hold the generative model and evaluation prompts fixed across methods and repeat answering/judging five times with memory stores and retrieved evidence fixed.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint details prompts, models and benchmark setup. No public implementation was located or independently reproduced in this review.
technical.strongest_baseline: LightMem is the strongest compared memory system by mean accuracy on LoCoMo; JustMem's paired comparison there has p=0.532. For LongMemEval-S, the paper reports 76.44% LightMem accuracy versus 83.40% JustMem. On LoCoMo-Plus, MemOS is the strongest baseline at 31.67% versus 62.59% for JustMem.

brief.title: JustMem reports adaptive long-term memory access with higher benchmark accuracy and lower model-token use
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported results generalize, separating broad evidence discovery from selective source replay could improve conversational recall while reducing generative-model token use. The result is meaningful for agent-memory design, but evidence comes from a bounded benchmark setup and does not measure total system cost.
